## Purpose and boundary

`buildAzureWorkspaceHostRoleDefinitions` in `packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/azure-connection.ts` prepares Azure CLI custom-role JSON from the same `AZURE_WORKSPACE_HOST_PERMISSION_ACTIONS` used by onboarding preflight. It never resolves credentials, creates a role, assigns access, spends cloud resources, publishes an image, or supplies live canary proof.

## Generate customer roles

Call the exported builder with the customer subscription UUID and an existing workspace resource-group name. Pass `imageResourceGroup` only when a managed image or Compute Gallery version lives in a different group in that same subscription. UUID and resource-group scope validation rejects wildcard/path-injection input; resource-group whitespace is refused. Secret-shaped fields are refused.

```ts
import { buildAzureWorkspaceHostRoleDefinitions } from './packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/azure-connection';
const roles = buildAzureWorkspaceHostRoleDefinitions({
  subscriptionId: '22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222', // replace with the customer subscription
  resourceGroup: 'papercusp-workspaces',
  imageResourceGroup: 'papercusp-images',
});
console.log(JSON.stringify(roles, null, 2));
```

Export each returned role object as its own JSON file. The subscription role contains subscription reads, provider read/register, SKU enumeration and regional quota reads. The lifecycle role contains the remaining resource permissions at the selected workspace resource group. Its three Key Vault key metadata/wrap/unwrap operations are `DataActions`; no secret-read permission or wildcard is emitted. The optional image-reader role grants only existing image/version reads at the separate image group. Neither the lifecycle role nor image reader receives subscription-wide assignability.

`AssignableScopes` declares where a role can be assigned; it is not an assignment. A customer administrator creates the roles using `az role definition create --role-definition @role.json`, retains the returned role-definition IDs, then assigns each role by ID to the intended principal at that role's sole `AssignableScopes[0]`. Use `az role assignment create --assignee-object-id <principal-object-id> --assignee-principal-type ServicePrincipal --role <role-definition-id> --scope <exact-scope>` for a service principal or managed identity; choose the correct principal type for a user. Run in the intended customer tenant and cloud. Role-definition creation requires the administrator's own roleDefinitions/write permission.

## Delegation review

The maintained lifecycle population includes roleAssignments/write and roleAssignments/delete. These are privileged operations: a principal may delegate additional access within the resource group. Vault write permissions also need customer review. The generated role is an exact, scoped permission template, not a claim that its principal cannot escalate or gain data access through delegation. Use a dedicated workspace group and review the customer's role-assignment conditions/delegated identities before assignment. The template does not create those conditions for the customer. Do not grant the lifecycle role at subscription scope. Customer-run resource-group creation precedes provisioning; the subscription role does not grant group create/delete across the subscription.

## Connection and preflight

Reuse `planAzureCredentialProvider` and `preflightAzureWorkspaceHostConnection`: local DefaultAzureCredential/Azure CLI, or the existing hosted federated-service-principal/managed-application contracts. Hosted identity remains secretless; keep runtime assertions and cloud credentials in approved references. Validate tenant/subscription identity, group existence, region/provider registration, every permission result, VM SKU, quota and image evidence. A generated JSON document or local fixture pass is not live Azure acceptance.

## Compute Gallery preparation

Reuse `executeAzureComputeGalleryRelease` in `azure-compute-gallery-release.ts`; do not invent a second image publisher. Supply publisher tenant/subscription, gallery/group/definition/version, source region, explicit target-region replication/storage policy, allowed readers and prior retained pins. Image publishing permissions belong to the publisher account; the customer image-reader template deliberately grants no gallery writes.

The existing release contract requires release-gate/build-manifest/signature/integrity and vulnerability-scan evidence, replicated availability, access checks and a clean-account launch. The clean-account subscription must differ from the publisher subscription and its region must be replicated. Prove that the consumer can boot the selected immutable gallery version with the required subnet/managed identity and no public IPv4, then retain its proof. New versions remain excluded from latest until the gated checks pass. Deprecate earlier versions without deleting pinned rollback versions. Cross-subscription/tenant gallery sharing requires the publisher's explicit access/sharing setup; this builder's optional image group is same-subscription only.

## Marketplace path and remaining publication prerequisites

The existing `AzureWorkspaceHostImageSelection` accepts publisher/offer/SKU/version plus an optional plan `{publisher, product, name}`. Select an explicit version and retain availability/architecture/plan agreement evidence from the actual customer account. Listing publication requires the authorized Partner Center publisher/account, approved offer/listing and legal/privacy/security receipts; role JSON and gallery fixtures do not establish any of those. Record unresolved publisher access, agreement, publication or external-review prerequisites on the carrier rather than declaring the Azure canary or commercial launch complete.

## Verification and acceptance

Focused verification: `npm run test:file -- packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/azure-connection.test.ts packages/operator-core/lib/workspace-host/azure-compute-gallery-release.test.ts`. The generator tests cover exact action parity, subscription/lifecycle separation, Key Vault DataActions, optional image-reader scope, invalid subscription/group scopes, secret rejection and independent returned arrays. Gallery tests cover the maintained release contract. A 2026-10-13 local run passed 31 tests (24 connection + 7 gallery), zero skipped, on local HEAD b01fcd34c9 with the connection test dirty; this is current working-tree proof, not committed/shipped or a live cloud result.
